- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or use lagged 3–5 day average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model shows persistent bias; apply mean reversion to 14-day moving average of historical prices.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizon are consistently too high in early cycles; apply downward bias of 1–3% relative to 18-day average of recent prices.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., -0.67 → 0.67), model lags in reaction; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true price movement.
